checks: The upper boundary is concave and upper semicontinuous on its compact projection. Minimizing the left slope quotient produces a support contact, and reflection supplies the right one. The two support lines majorize the old roof on their respective sides; old secants at the contacts and the slope drop at the apex establish concavity of the joined graph.

The bound by the slope to the old endpoint gives negative contact height at most ε times its horizontal distance from that endpoint divided by the apex distance. Compactness puts every limit contact on the original face, hence each contact tends to its endpoint and has height o(ε).

The apex lies in the convex vertical Minkowski extrusion A+[0,εe₂]. Vertical sections therefore add at most ε and have unchanged lower endpoints. The contact positions bound the horizontal extent of the addition, giving o(ε) gain off the face. Dividing the new roof over the face by ε gives uniform convergence to the tent.

A transverse line has only an O(ε)-length possible indicator-change strip along the old face for shifts of size O(ε). A parallel proper cut is separated from the face line and has fixed membership on the gain band. Thus both types give the same uniform first-order formula.

For a polygon, the apex retains every other facet inequality and violates only the displayed support. Each entering segment crosses that support inside its entire original face. The excess is the indicated triangle, matching source 6e9992972c414d73 §§1–2.
